result.rationale: The diff line `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` is tautological: when externalCalendarId is falsy, the find predicate can never match (comparing externalId against a falsy value it was filtered on), so calendarId becomes undefined. Old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Google's deleteEvent then receives calendarId undefined instead of the previous fallback, breaking deletion when callers omit externalCalendarId.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now derive the fallback calendar id using `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. If `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, that `find` predicate can’t match any real calendar `externalId`, so the result becomes `undefined`. Unlike `createEvent` (which does `selectedCalendar || "primary"`), the shown `deleteEvent` code computes `calendarId` without a correct fallback and appears poised to pass an undefined calendarId to Google API calls, breaking deletions/updates when callers omit `externalCalendarId` (which can happen per the diff’s cancellation paths passing possibly-missing `externalCalendarId`).
